content: The Handbook for Guideline Development (second edition) was accessed on July 19, 2022, via the WHO IRIS platform. The WHO's 2015 recommendations on interventions to improve preterm birth outcomes were reviewed in a document accessed on August 4, 2022. Balshem et al. (2011) discussed the GRADE guidelines for rating the quality of evidence in the Journal of Clinical Epidemiology. Zahroh et al. (2022) conducted a systematic review and narrative synthesis on factors influencing the appropriate use of interventions for managing preterm birth, published in PLoS Medicine. Sebastian et al. (2022) reviewed the cost-effectiveness of antenatal corticosteroids and tocolytics in preterm birth management. Schünemann et al. (2013) provided insights into the GRADE Working Group's methodologies. Higgins et al. (2021) updated their systematic review methods in February 2021. Huseerau et al. (2013) introduced the CHEERS statement for health economic evaluation reporting in the BMJ. Alonso-Coello et al. (2013) described the GRADE Evidence-to-Decision frameworks for healthcare decision-making. Hilton Boon et al. (2021) addressed challenges in applying the GRADE approach to public health guidelines. The WHO's 2022 recommendations on tocolytics for preterm birth outcomes and antenatal care for a positive pregnancy experience were highlighted. Early essential newborn care guidelines were also reviewed. The guideline development group (GDG) included experts such as Shabina Ariff, Elena Atteva, Maria Laura Costa, Gary Darmstadt, Bissallah Ekele, David Haas, Caroline Homer, Jeeva Sankar, Joy Lawn, Pisake Lumbiganon, Silke Mader, Elizabeth Molyneux, Ashraf Nabhan, Hiromi Obara, Zahida Qureshi, Khalid Yunis, and Hoang Thi Tran. Their expertise spanned neonatology, obstetrics, midwifery, and public health. Some members declared interests, such as involvement in trials or research grants, which were managed to avoid conflicts during guideline formulation. The Evidence Synthesis Group (ESG) included Meghan Bohren, Jenny Cao, Leanne Jones, Frances Kellie, Jen Ramson, Joshua Vogel, and Myfanwy Williams. They contributed to evidence synthesis and guideline methodology. Joshua Vogel and Zahida Qureshi declared involvement in the WHO ACTION-I trial, with measures in place to manage potential conflicts. The WHO Steering Group and external review group included experts like Edgardo Abalos, Philippa Middleton, Suneeta Mittal, Siddarth Ramji, and Haroon Saloojee, who provided additional expertise in obstetrics, neonatology, and public health.
